plain_english: Arjuna asks which devotees are most accomplished in yoga, those who worship the Lord or those who worship the unmanifest.
sanskrit_cite: atha dvādaśo'dhyāyaḥ   arjuna uvāca   evaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktāstvāṃ paryupāsate | ye  cāpyakṣaramavyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ | evam-uktena nayena ye seśvarabrahmopāsakāḥ ye ca  kevalamātmamātra-mupāsate teṣāṃ viśeṣākhyānāya praśnaḥ

plain_english: The Lord declares that devotees who enter him with mind and worship him with supreme faith are most united.
sanskrit_cite: śrībhagavānuvāca   mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate | śraddhayā  parayopetāste me yuktatamā matāḥ | māheśvaryaviṣayo yeṣāṃ samāveśaḥ-akṛtrimastanmayībhāvaḥ te  yuktatamā mama matāḥ-ityanena pratijñā kriyate

plain_english: Those who worship the imperishable, indescribable, unmanifest, all-pervading, inconceivable, unchanging, immovable, and firm.
sanskrit_cite: ye tvakṣaramanirdeśyamavyaktaṃ paryupāsate | sarvatragamacintyaṃ ca  kūṭasthamacalaṃ dhruvam

plain_english: By restraining the senses and being equal-minded everywhere, devoted to all beings' welfare, they attain me alone.
sanskrit_cite: sanniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ | te prāpnuvanti  māmeva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ

plain_english: The unmanifest path is hard for embodied beings; even Brahman-worshippers attain the Lord, but with greater effort.
sanskrit_cite: kleśo'dhikatarasteṣāmavyaktāsaktacetasām | avyaktā hi  gatirduḥkhaṃ dehabhṛdbhiravāpyate | ye punarakṣaraṃ brahmopāsate ātmānaṃ  sarvatragam-ityādibhirviśeṣaṇairātmanaḥ sarve īśvaradharmā  āropyante | ato brahmopāsakā api māmeva yadyapi yānti  tathāpyadhikatarasteṣāṃ kleśaḥ | ātmani  kilāpahatapāpmatvādiguṇāṣṭakāropaṃ vidhāya  paścāttamevopāsate iti svataḥsiddhaguṇagrāmagarimaṇi  īśvare'yatnasādhye sthite'pi dviguṇamāyāsaṃ vindanti

plain_english: Those who renounce all actions into me, devoted to me, meditate on me through yoga and worship.
sanskrit_cite: ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ | ananyenaiva  yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate

plain_english: For those whose minds are fixed in me, I, O Partha, become the deliverer from the ocean of death and samsara, and not after a long time.
sanskrit_cite: teṣāmahaṃ samuddhartā mṛtyusaṃsārasāgarāt | bhavāmi na  cirātpārtha mayyāveśitacetasām

plain_english: Place your mind in me alone and fix your intellect in me; you will dwell in me, abiding in supreme yoga. Those who renounce everything in me through the previously stated teaching are rescued by me from all obstacles and afflictions. The entering of mind is explained. This yoga is supreme because it is unartificial. When knowledge is awakened through the manifestation of distinguished means, posture, abiding, and samadhi possibility in my hymn, that is not your ever-flowing innate consciousness; because of the triad's presence, consciousness is clearly perceived here too. But when fuel-less, taking self-mastery and indifference to the body, consciousness suddenly knows itself and the fire of knowledge arises at once. Then, goddess, free from the supports of that body-person, one knows the great lord, who agitates the bonds of the powerless, and so forth.
sanskrit_cite: mayyeva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya | nivatsyasi tvaṃ  mayyeva yogamuttamamāsthiḥ | prāguktopadeśena tu ye sarvaṃ mayi saṃnyasyanti teṣāmahaṃ  samuddhartā-sakalavighnādikleśebhyaḥ | cetasa āveśanaṃ  vyākhyātam | tathā ca eṣa evottamo yogo'kṛtrimatvāt | tathā ca  mama stotre-   viśiṣṭakaraṇāsanasthitisamādhisaṃbhāvanā- vibhāvitatayā yadā  kamapi bodhamullāsayet | na sā tava sadoditā svarasavāhinī yā  citi- yatastritayasaṃnidhau sphuṭamihāpi saṃvedyate | yadā tu vigatendhanaḥ svavaśavartitāṃ  saṃśraya-nnakṛtrimasamullasatpulakakampabāṣpānugaḥ | śarīranirapekṣatāṃ sphuṭamupādadānaścitaḥ svayaṃ jhagiti  budhyate yugapadeva bodhānalaḥ | tadaiva tava devi  tadvapuruṣāśrayairvarjitaṃ maheśamavabudhyate  vivaśapāśasaṃkṣobhakam | ityādi

plain_english: You cannot make the mind enter steadily into me by practice-yoga alone; then, O Dhanañjaya, to obtain me, without intense descent of divine power and long-pleased guru foot grace, absorption is difficult—thus practice.
sanskrit_cite: ahāveśayituṃ cittaṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram | abhyāsayogena tato  māmicchāptuṃ dhanañjaya | tīvratarabhagavacchaktipātaṃ cirataraprasāditagurucaraṇānugrahaṃ  ca vinā durlabha āveśaḥ-ityabhyāsaḥ

plain_english: Even if you cannot practice, be devoted to right action; by performing actions for my sake you will attain perfection. Since practice is hindered by obstacles, therefore perform actions, worship, recitation, study, sacrifice, and the like to destroy them.
sanskrit_cite: abhyāse'pyasamarthoḥ sanmatkarmaparamo bhava | madarthamapi karmāṇi  kurvansiddhimavāpsyasi | abhyāso'pi na śakyate-vighnādyabhibhavāt | atastannāśāya  karma-pūjājapasvādhyāyahomādīn kuru

plain_english: Even if you are established in my yoga but unable to do this, renounce the fruits of all actions and remain self-controlled. If, from ignorance, you cannot perform divine action, then renounce all of it to me through self-offering, according to the method stated in scripture. Relying on that intent, I have spoken in an easy procedure. Whatever is deficient, excessive, unknown, lacking sequence, lacking attention, or a slip of intellect, forgive mercifully, O Shambhu, since you are full of compassion. By this yoga of hymn I offer your self; again, causelessly, I attain fitness for sufferings. In the supreme lordly doctrinal scriptures, this very intent is that of self-offering; this meaning is summarized.
sanskrit_cite: athaitadapyaśakto'si kartuṃ madyogamāsthitaḥ | sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān | yadi ca bhagavatkarma kartuṃ na śakto'si-ajñatvāt  śāstroktakramāvedanāt | tatsarvaṃ mayi saṃnyaseḥ  ātmanivedanadvāreṇetyāśayaḥ | amumevāśayamāśritya  laghuprakriyāyāṃ mayaivoktaṃ-   ūnādhikamavijñātaṃ paurvāparyavivarjitam | yaccāvadhānarahitaṃ  buddherviskhalitaṃ ca yat | tatsarve mama sarveśa bhaktasyārtasya  durmateḥ | kṣantavyaṃ kṛpayā śaṃbho yatastvaṃ karuṇāparaḥ | anena stotrayogena tavātmānaṃ nivedaye | punarniṣkāraṇamahaṃ  duḥkhānāṃ naimi pātratām | iti | pārameśvareṣu hi siddhāntaśāstreṣu  ātmanivedane'yamevābhiprāyaḥ | tadidaṃ tātparyamupasaṃhriyate-

plain_english: Knowledge is better than practice; meditation surpasses knowledge; from meditation comes renunciation of fruits and then peace. Since knowledge is absorption and practice's fruit is absorption, meditation as divine fullness is distinguished and attains desired realization; then action-fruits can be renounced, otherwise renunciation is nowhere; ultimate peace follows renunciation. Therefore absorption-natured knowledge, root of all, is principal.
sanskrit_cite: śreyo hi jñānamabhyāsājjñānāddhyānaṃ viśiṣyate | dhyānātkarmaphalatyāgastyāgācchāntiranantarā | jñānam-āveśātma abhyāsācchreyaḥ-abhyāsasya tatphalatvāt | tasmādevāveśāt dhyānaṃ-bhagavanmayatvaṃ viśiṣyate-viśeṣatvaṃ  yāti-abhimataprāptyā | sati dhyāne-bhagavanmayatve karmaphalāni  saṃnyasituṃ yujyante | anyathājñātarūpe kva saṃnyāsaḥ | karmaphalatyāge ca ātyantikī śāntiḥ | ataḥ  sarvamūlatvādāveśātmakaṃ jñānameva pradhānam

plain_english: The devotee who does not hate any being, is friendly and compassionate, free of mine-ness and ego, equal in pain and joy, and forgiving is dear to the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca | nirmamo  nirahaṅkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī | maitrī-amatsaratā yasyāstīti | evaṃ karuṇaḥ | mamāmī-ityādiḥ  mamakāraḥ ahamudāro'haṃ tejasvī ahaṃ sahanaḥ-ityādiḥ  ahaṃkāraḥ-etau yasya na staḥ | kṣamā-apakāriṇaṃ śatruṃ  pratyadveṣabuddhiḥ

plain_english: The yogi who is always content, self-controlled, firmly resolved, and has offered mind and intellect to the Lord is dear to the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: santuṣṭaḥ satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ | mayyarpitamanobuddhiryo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ | satataṃ yogī-vyavahārāvasthāyāmapi praśāntāntaḥ karaṇatvāt

plain_english: He who does not agitate the world, is not agitated by it, and is freed from joy, anger, fear, and agitation is dear to the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ | harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ

plain_english: The devotee who expects nothing, is pure and skillful, remains indifferent, is free from pain, and renounces the fruits of all undertakings is dear to the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: anapekṣaḥ śucirdakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ | sarvārambhaphalatyāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ

plain_english: He who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor desires, and renounces the fruits of good and bad is dear to the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati | śubhāśubhaphalatyāgī bhaktimānyaḥ sa me priyaḥ

plain_english: Equal toward enemy and friend, in honor and dishonor, in cold, heat, pleasure, and pain, and free from attachment.
sanskrit_cite: samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāvamānayoḥ | śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ

plain_english: One who is equal in blame and praise, silent, content with anything, homeless, steady-minded, and devoted is dear to me.
sanskrit_cite: tulyanindāstutirmaunī santuṣṭo yenakenacit | aniketaḥ  sthiramatirbhaktimānme priyo naraḥ

plain_english: Those who faithfully practice this immortal dharma are exceedingly dear; one without fixed resolve, accepting what comes and absorbed in the supreme Lord, easily attains supreme isolation.
sanskrit_cite: ye tu dharmyāmṛtamidaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate | śraddadhānā  matparamā bhaktāste'tīva me priyāḥ | aniketaḥ-idameva mayā kartavyam-iti yasya nāsti pratijñā | yathāprāptahevākitayā sukhaduḥkhādikamupabhujjānaḥ  parameśvaraviṣayasamāveśitahṛdayaḥ sukhenaiva prāpnoti  paramakaivalyamiti śivam

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: the wealth of absorption born from supreme bliss is itself Brahman-being in all states, attained without effort.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   paramānandavaivaśyasañjātāveśasaṃpadaḥ | svayaṃ  sarvāsvavasthāsu brahmasattā hyayatnataḥ | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe dvādaśo'dhyāyaḥ
